title: Swe mid systemdesign rate limiter
question: Design a rate limiter for a public API, so one client can't send more than, say, 100 requests per minute.
idealAnswer:
Picks and explains an algorithm, e.g. token bucket or sliding window, over a naive fixed-window counter, and can explain fixed window's boundary burst problem (a client can send 2x the limit right around a window edge)

Recognizes that because there are multiple server instances, an in-memory per-instance counter won't correctly enforce a shared limit, and proposes a shared store like Redis to hold counts/timestamps

Addresses atomicity of the increment-and-check operation in the shared store, so concurrent requests from the same client near the limit don't all get let through due to a race

Defines what happens when the limit is hit: returning 429 Too Many Requests, ideally with a Retry-After header so the client knows when to try again

Bonus: mentions keying the limit appropriately, e.g. per API key or per user rather than per IP alone, since IPs can be shared (NAT, corporate networks) or spoofed
